edits.old: SERVER-14322 documents a specific automatic DuplicateKey retry path for upsert:true after a unique-index conflict when the operation is not a multi-update, the predicate is one equality or an AND of equalities over exactly the index fields, and the update leaves those fields unchanged. The ticket says this fix shipped in MongoDB 4.1.6 and later. SERVER-94156 reports a collation limitation in the behavior it tracks: the retry check compares the index key with the query predicate, and a collated index key is a CollationKey rather than a raw value. The ticket lists fixes in 8.1.0-rc0, 8.0.5, and 7.0.21. MongoDB's manual states that starting in 8.1, an upsert in a multi-document transaction does not retry after a duplicate key error. These scoped server behaviors do not justify blanket application retries for E11000. (medium confidence)
edits.new: SERVER-14322 documents that, via SERVER-37124 (fixed in 4.1.6 and later), the server automatically retries an upsert after a DuplicateKey error when the operation has upsert:true, is not a multi-update, the match condition is a single equality or an AND of equalities over exactly the index key pattern fields, and the update does not mutate those fields. SERVER-94156 reports that when the unique index has a collation the retry check never passes, because the index key is a CollationKey rather than a raw value; its fix versions are 8.1.0-rc0, 8.0.5 and 7.0.21. MongoDB's manual states that starting in 8.1, an upsert in a multidocument transaction does not retry after a duplicate key error. These scoped server behaviors do not justify blanket application retries for E11000. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-14322 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-94156 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md

evidence.quote: As part of SERVER-37124, fixed in versions 4.1.6 and later, the server will automatically retry performing the upsert in cases where it is detectably safe to do so.
The set of fields over which there is an equality predicate equals the set of fields in the index key pattern kp.
But if index has collation, the key there would be CollationKey, not raw value. So this check is never passed.
Starting in MongoDB 8.1, if an `upsert` operation runs in a multidocument transaction, then the `upsert` does not retry when it encounters a duplicate key error.
